slides.title: Watching Practice As It Happens
bullets: Observational studies don't assign the intervention, they observe natural clinical practice
They answer questions RCTs can't or shouldn't answer
MSLs encounter this evidence constantly at congresses and in publications

slides.title: Cohort, Case-Control and Cross-Sectional
bullets: Cohort studies follow exposed and unexposed groups over time, comparing incidence
Cohort studies can be prospective, recruited before the outcome occurs, or retrospective
Case-control studies start from the outcome and compare cases to controls, suiting rare outcomes
Cross-sectional studies measure exposure and outcome at one point in time, a prevalence snapshot

slides.title: Closer to Real Clinical Practice
bullets: Observational data includes comorbidities, polypharmacy and diverse patients trials tend to exclude
Valuable for understanding effectiveness rather than controlled efficacy
Detects long-term safety signals a short trial could miss
Covers rare populations or outcomes a randomized trial could never afford to study

slides.title: Confounding Is the Core Weakness
bullets: Without randomization, compared groups can differ systematically in ways that also affect the outcome
Those differences can be mistaken for a treatment effect
Multivariate adjustment and propensity score matching reduce but never fully eliminate this risk

slides.title: Naming the Design, Choosing the Words
bullets: Quickly identify whether a study is cohort, case-control or cross-sectional
Know what question that design can reasonably answer
Communicate results as association and higher likelihood, never causality or demonstrated effect

takeaway.title: Observational studies show what happens in real practice, not proof of cause and effect
bullets: Cohort, case-control and cross-sectional designs each answer a different kind of question
Confounding is the central limitation, and statistical adjustment only reduces it
The right language is association and likelihood, never causality or demonstrated effect
